title: Foreign-Field Points Accumulation Envy
pattern: An outer struct method increments a local accumulator based on checks against multiple nested fields of an associated struct.
why_bad: This creates a deep logical dependency on the internal business rules of the referenced struct. The calculation of how many loyalty points a rental is worth belongs with the rental, not with the statement printer.
detection: An accumulator variable in a loop where the increment logic relies entirely on conditional checks on properties of the loop item.
counterexample: Accumulating a simple count of elements or summing a direct primitive getter (e.g., `r.days_rented`) without conditional business logic.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring* (1999), Chapter 1 and Chapter 3 ("Feature Envy").
